newsitem.title: UK: AMB - Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 17.
newsitem.headline: AMB - Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 17.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - The divorce finalised last week between French advertising group Publicis and True North in the U.S. will allow Publicis to expand its worldwide network and make up for lost time, analysts and industry experts say.

HANOVER - Private German TV broadcaster RTL is fined more than 19 million marks ($11 million) after a federal state court rules that it showed too many commercials during its films. The channel was found to have breached advertising regulations on more than 30 occasions between 1993 and 1994.

ROCHESTER, New York - Eastman Kodak Co says it is assigning all product and service advertising for its Kodak film and cameras to Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide, dropping its long-time ad agency J. Walter Thompson. "This switch in advertising assignments for Kodak consumer products reflects our need for a new creative focus and direction," says Carl Gustin, Kodak's chief marketing officer.

MAINZ, Germany - TV commercials in Germany reach 86 percent of viewers of the programme during which they are shown, according to a study by the Sat. 1 commercial channel. Only one in nine viewers who took part on the 1996 survey switched channels or turned the television off during commercial breaks.

WASHINGTON - The top communications regulator in the U.S., Federal Communications Commission Chairman Reed Hundt, who was forced to scrap plans to investigate liquor advertising on television this month, vows to reexamine the issue in July. Last year the liquor industry in the U.S. abandoned a decades-old voluntary ban on marketing over the airwaves.

LONDON - The European Advertising Tripartite, a trade group representing advertisers, ad agencies and media in Europe, names Florence Ranson, former manager of a European Commission information and communication project, as its secretary general.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - German media giant Bertelsmann AG and Bavarian rival Leo Kirch are in intensive negotiations that could lead to close cooperation between their joint pay TV channel Premiere and Kirch's DF1, the companies say.

WASHINGTON - The White House says it has not changed its stance on restricting the availability of pornography to children on the Internet, but is weighing what to do if the Supreme Court strikes down a law that limits such access.

LONDON - British Sky Broadcasting Group says Chief Executive Sam Chisholm will step down at the end of the year on medical advice. The satellite television operator, 40-percent owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, named Mark Booth, chief operating officer of Japan's Japan Sky Broadcasting, to replace Chisholm as from January 1, 1998.

TOKYO - Sony Corp says it will provide products and technology to NBC of the United States for its coverage of future Olympic Games, and to France's TVRS 98 for its coverage of soccer's 1998 World Cup.

BURLINGTON, Massachusetts - Individual Inc, the electronic publisher, agrees to a definitive deal to buy ClariNet Communications Corp, an Internet news company, for about 1.5 million individual shares, or $7.7 million.

BOSTON - The Christian Science church says it has failed to sell Monitor Radio and the news network used by more than 200 public radio stations in the United States will stop broadcasting at the end of this month.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

LONDON - The judge in the libel case pitting McDonald's fast food chain against two penniless activists is expected to deliver his verdict this week, ending what is described in the Guinness Book of Records as England's longest ever trial.
LONDON - British drinks group Allied Domecq Plc forms joint venture with Indian company Clan Morgan & Co to build a plant in India to bottle Teacher's Whisky.

WASHINGTON - U.S. business leaders believe that they face unfair barriers in Japan's market and that Tokyo is not doing enough to address those concerns, according to a survey released by the Economic Strategy Institute think tank.
ADELAIDE - Mildara Blass, the wine division of Foster's Brewing Group, says it is setting up a joint venture in Chile and winemaking operations in the United States.

LONDON - Robert Earl, president and chief executive of Planet Hollywood International Inc, the restaurant chain, is planning to set up new restaurants in London and New York with a rock music theme, the Guardian newspaper reports.
MEXICO CITY - Mexican beer exports reached $52.8 million in April, the highest monthly total since 1980, Mexico's national statistics institute says.

FRANKFURT - The head of German car maker Opel AG says the company will defend its top European market position despite plans by parent General Motors Corp to use Opel to launch an ambitious global expansion plan. A German magazine said earlier that GM officials in Europe criticised the expansion strategy, saying GM needed to devote more resources to European product development and quality measures.
TOKYO - Japanese electronics giant Toshiba Corp unveils the latest in a series of new miniaturised electronic gadgets -- a business card-sized digital camera called the Allegretto.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

HONG KONG - Five years ago, the crowds in Hong Kong's trendiest clubs were 90 percent Western. Today they are 90 percent Chinese. The dance culture that has spawned a musical explosion in Britain has infiltrated Hong Kong, ushering in fashion trends, a growing appetite for European music and a surge in drug use.

LONDON - Micro Compact Car AG, makers of the tiny Smart car, say it is a revolution in the making which will change urban motoring forever. But detractors say the vehicle is too small, too expensive and too ugly. The diminutive two-seater is aimed at helping solve the problem of urban traffic.
ABIDJAN - The Ivory Coast, the world's largest cocoa maker, is expanding production to meet world demand.
